title: The Double Debt Again
premise: Petra Blackwood, a whistle-blower living under four names, has spent five years ghosting through Europe's gray markets, solving deniable problems for people who pay in silence. When a burner phone that shouldn't exist rings with the voice of his presumed-dead sister, he learns she faked her death to infiltrate a tri-government data-sharing program—and she's about to be erased for what she found. To save her, Petra must smuggle proof of an illegal assassination ledger past three intelligence services and the assassin hunting them both, a man who once trained him. In the end, Petra trades his own anonymity—his last and greatest asset—to expose the ledger, choosing family over invisibility as the truth detonates across three governments.
about_author: Mara Sterling is a former investigative journalist who spent a decade covering intelligence scandals before turning to fiction. She writes from a different city every few months, a habit she insists is research rather than paranoia.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Address
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Working under his fourth identity in Lisbon, Petra quietly dismantles a corrupt shipping contract for a client who will never admit hiring him. The chapter establishes his tradecraft, his loneliness, and his rule: never leave a thread someone can pull. The beat is controlled isolation—until a burner phone appears in his safe house, one he never bought.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The phone rings; the voice belongs to Nadia, his sister, dead by official record for five years. She gives him ninety seconds of instructions and a warning: they know the phone exists. Petra verifies her voiceprint against childhood memories and realizes his invisibility was always someone else's design. The beat is vertigo—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What Nadia Found
chapters.summary: POV Nadia, via intercepted audio diary. From inside the Meridian Accord's Vienna facility, Nadia describes the ledger: three governments outsourcing assassinations through a shared black account. Her handlers are closing in. The chapter reframes Petra's exile—he was burned years ago to bury her trail. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Trained Him
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In Prague, Petra meets his old handler, Ilya Sorokin, to trade favors for access—and finds the assassin Kessler already there, waiting politely. Kessler offers Petra a clean exit if he walks away. Petra refuses and barely escapes, learning Kessler isn't freelance: he answers to the ledger itself. The beat is the past becoming a weapon pointed at him.

chapters.title: Found Family, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. Petra calls in debts from the only people who ever felt like family: a forger named June, a disgraced analyst named Okafor, and a retired courier with bad lungs. Assembling them in a Rotterdam safehouse, he admits how much he needs them—a first. The beat is warmth kindling inside fear; belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV Okafor. The team maps the Accord's structure and discovers the ledger is scheduled to be 'consolidated'—every loose end, including Nadia, eliminated within nine days. Okafor wrestles with rejoining the system that ruined him versus burning it down. The beat is the ticking clock made personal: duty to institutions versus duty to people.

chapters.title: Vienna, After Midnight
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The extraction of Nadia goes wrong when Kessler anticipates their route; June takes a bullet covering the retreat, and Petra reaches his sister at last—only to find she won't leave without the ledger copy still locked inside the facility. The beat is love colliding with mission, each willing to die for the other's choice.

chapters.title: The Price of Proof
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. Hiding in a flooded tram depot, brother and sister finally speak honestly—about the death she staged, the life he abandoned, the parents' funeral neither attended together. They plan the impossible: broadcast the ledger through three national systems simultaneously so no single government can bury it. The beat is reconciliation forged into strategy.

chapters.title: Everything He Was
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The climax: to authenticate the leak, Petra must surrender his real identity—name, biometrics, history—to the world, making himself permanently findable. He triggers the broadcast while Kessler closes in; June's forgery buys seconds, Okafor's contacts buy reach, and Petra faces Kessler unarmed, daring him to kill a man the whole world is now watching. The beat is sacrifice as victory.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Having
chapters.summary: POV Petra, epilogue. Three governments reel; the ledger's architects are indicted or vanished; Kessler disappears into the machinery he served. Petra, publicly named and legally alive for the first time in years, sits with Nadia and the wounded-but-recovering June in a Lisbon café—visible, vulnerable, and no longer alone. The beat is belonging earned at full price, and peace that cost everything but was worth it.
